top.line: Five manual stages today; the Factory does them once, so it scales
top.para: My setup guide puts a website and a local model on a Pi from a Mac in five stages, each with a choice where an owner can give up. The idea is to turn it round: the Factory builds and tests one image, a small part is written per unit, and the owner plugs in two cables and opens a page.

in-short.line: Five stages today; one tested image and two cables tomorrow
in-short.para: The guide works but is full of choices. The Factory does the work once as an image, writes a small per-unit part, and the Wi-Fi can be set the way a printer does it. Every unit is the same, so it scales; for the Kickstarter we promise a box that works. Nothing is built yet.

today.line: Five stages from a Mac, all in the official guide
today.para: Image the card with Raspberry Pi Imager (OS Lite 64-bit, hostname, user, Wi-Fi, SSH), boot, connect over SSH at hostname.local, update, then add the site and a model that fits the memory. Checked against the official getting-started page: the 27W supply, Imager's settings, OS Lite, .local.

choices.line: Every choice in the guide is a place someone stops
choices.para: The right drive, a host key, a hidden password, the router's device list, a runtime that depends on the site, a model that fits the memory. A sovereign website is for people who want their website, not a Linux machine, so the question is who should follow the guide.

factory.line: The Factory does the guide once, as a tested image
factory.para: Stage one becomes the image, stage four is done before shipping with signed updates after, and stage five is decided because the Factory built the site and measured the model. The image is tested on a real Pi, the same move as the SGit server factory.

per-unit.line: One shared image, a small per-unit part, no secrets baked
per-unit.para: The OS, runtime, web server, model and update timer go in the image; hostname, site and keys are written per unit, and each unit makes its own host key. The Wi-Fi can be set like a printer: the Pi opens a setup network, the owner gives it the home Wi-Fi from a phone.

owner.line: The owner plugs in, opens a page, sees the website
owner.para: Power and a cable, or the Pi's own setup network from a phone; a few minutes; a page showing the website served from the shelf. On the Pro tier the same page builds the site with the local model. No Terminal, and shutdown becomes a button.

scales.line: It scales because every unit is the same unit
scales.para: A guide makes a different Pi each time. An image makes the same one: test it once and every card is tested, fix a fault once and send it to all as a signed update, while the agents run updates, monitoring and backups the same way everywhere.

kickstarter.line: The campaign promises a box that works, not a guide
kickstarter.para: This is how the plan's two Pi tiers can be made. A backer can believe a box that works when plugged in, the video shows exactly that, and the risks are short. The guide stays published for anyone doing it by hand, and as the image's specification.

now.line: Guide done; next, one card from a first image, timed
now.para: The guide exists and matches the official documentation; the appliance does not exist yet. Next: one card written by the Factory, put in the experiment's Pi 5 and timed from power to website, then the experiment's measurements, then a second card to show it is the same.

limits.line: A plan: nothing imaged, measured or submitted yet
limits.para: The appliance, the image's contents and the setup network are proposals; the steps were checked against the official pages, not every network; no model is measured; the tiers are the 19 November plan and nothing is submitted to Kickstarter; public access and selling hardware are covered elsewhere.

sources.line: My setup guide and words of 22 November 2026
sources.para: My Raspberry Pi setup guide and my words to the newsroom's agents on 22 November 2026, written up by newsroom.c in my voice; the steps checked against the official getting-started and configuration pages; the tiers and the experiment from the articles of 19 November.
